title: Galle vs Mirissa: Which Should You Visit?
verdict: Galle for history, food, and a sophisticated base. Mirissa for whale watching, beach vibes, and Coconut Tree Hill. Do both — they're 30 km apart.

categories.name: Beaches
categories.summary: Mirissa has the better beach right on its doorstep. Galle's best beach is Unawatuna, 4 km away.

categories.name: Cultural Attractions
categories.summary: Galle Fort is a UNESCO World Heritage Site. Mirissa has minimal cultural attractions.

categories.name: Food Scene
categories.summary: Galle has the best restaurant scene on Sri Lanka's south coast. Mirissa is adequate but simpler.

categories.name: Cost
categories.summary: Mirissa is 20-30% cheaper. Budget travelers can do $25-35/day; Galle runs $50-90.

categories.name: Wildlife
categories.summary: Blue whale watching from Mirissa is world-class. Peak season November-April.

categories.name: Nightlife
categories.summary: Mirissa has beach bars and bonfire nights. Galle has rooftop cocktail bars.

categories.name: Getting There
categories.summary: Direct scenic train from Colombo to Galle (2.5h, $1.40-4). Mirissa requires a connection via Galle.

faq.question: Should I stay in Galle or Mirissa?
faq.answer: Most travelers base in Galle and day-trip to Mirissa. They're 30 km apart. Add 2 nights in Mirissa if whale watching is a priority.

faq.question: How far is Mirissa from Galle?
faq.answer: 30 km, about 40 minutes by bus (LKR 80-100) or 30 minutes by tuk-tuk ($6-8).

faq.question: Is Mirissa good for whale watching?
faq.answer: Yes — one of the world's best. Blue whales November-April, peak January-March. Shared boat ~$30-35.
